title: Generic field of normalization in an algebraic extension
statement: Let $Z$ be an integral scheme with function field $K$ [def-sc-function-field], and let $L/K$ be an algebraic field extension. Let $Z^L$ be its normalization in $L$, and $a:\operatorname{Spec}L\to Z^L$ the canonical map [def-fin-normalization-extension]. There is an isomorphism $e:\operatorname{Spec}L\cong\operatorname{Spec}K(Z^L)$ such that $a$ equals $e$ followed by the generic-point morphism of $Z^L$.

proof.text: Use the existing proved theorem Scheme.exists_iso_toNormalization_normalizationIn. On a nonempty affine chart with ring A, every element of L integral over A is in the image of the generic stalk of the normalization, by normalizationObjIso. Every algebraic element of L has a nonzero A-multiple integral over A. Thus that generic stalk maps surjectively onto L, and injectivity follows because it is a map of fields. The resulting Spec isomorphism commutes with the canonical generic map. No new Lean proof or axiom is introduced.
